riskAssessment.reason: The scheduler is a small application boundary, but incorrect weekday semantics or Domain coupling could trigger reports at the wrong cadence.
riskAssessment.reviewNotes: The roadmap specifies a default weekend run and configurable day_of_week. A pure injected weekday decision boundary is sufficient; runtime timers and persisted run history are explicitly out of scope.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The default Weekly Scheduler is due on its configured weekend day.
scenarioCoverage.expected: A default scheduler uses Sunday and returns Due for Sunday while remaining NotDue on another weekday.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Evaluate the default scheduler against Sunday and Saturday with deterministic weekday values.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A configured day_of_week changes the trigger day without changing Domain behavior.
scenarioCoverage.expected: A schedule configured for Monday returns Due only for Monday and exposes the configuration unchanged.

acceptance: The application-level WeeklyScheduler API exposes a default Sunday weekend cadence and a configurable day_of_week.
The scheduler returns a deterministic, structured Due or NotDue decision for an observed Weekday and retains the relevant weekday values.
The scheduler is a trigger boundary only; it does not calculate, persist, render, publish, retry, or mutate Weekly Radar Domain data.
Module-local and public integration tests cover default cadence, all configured weekdays, stable decisions, and the non-due path without real runtime, network, or secret values.
Architecture verification proves the Weekly Radar Domain remains independent from Scheduler and infrastructure concerns.
Scheduler specification/plan, reference-impact evidence, strict Finish/Archive, and the authorized publish/merge/close lifecycle pass.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.
Keep the scheduler in the Application boundary and keep Domain free of Scheduler, Telegram, HTTP, persistence, and secret dependencies.
Keep the trigger deterministic and injectable; do not read system time or environment configuration inside the scheduling decision.
Do not add a new Work Item for issues discovered inside this scope; correct them in WR-013 when safe and relevant.

intent.problem: The Weekly Radar roadmap has a weekly execution sequence but no explicit, testable scheduler boundary. Without one, a future runner could scatter weekday logic into Domain or accidentally run the report on the wrong day.
constraints: Implement only an application-level scheduling decision boundary with a configurable day_of_week and a weekend default.
Use explicit Weekday values supplied by an outer runtime so tests do not depend on the machine clock, timezone, CI environment, or external services.
Do not own persistence, deduplication history, report calculation, rendering, publication, retry, or Telegram configuration in this WI.
Preserve the existing DDD/Clean Architecture boundary: Scheduler may trigger the use case, but Domain must not know Scheduler exists.
Complete TDD, focused/module-local/integration verification, strict Finish/Archive, local commit, publish, merge, close, and branch cleanup under the recorded lifecycle.
intent.rationale: A small pure application boundary makes the weekly cadence explicit and auditable while leaving runtime orchestration and research decisions outside the Domain.
